hypothesis: C: F-BERT alpha (ev^0.35) on the correlation matrix, on top of the current chain
origin: the instruction C hypothesis, which died on <pod> at 2026-11-15 on a broadcasting bug (V * clip(ev)**0.35, shapes (753,400,400) x (753,400)) and was never retried. It also targeted the old 0.6927 chain; this runs it against the current 0.7326.
verdict: FAILS AT EVERY WEIGHT. Raising the correlation matrix eigenvalues to 0.35 (F-BERT exponent) and mixing into the certified kernel is monotonically worse as its weight grows: -0.0003 at 10 %, -0.0009 at 25 %, -0.0025 at 50 %, -0.0079 alone (0/60, p 0.046).
why: the certified chain already passes the correlation edges through a partial-correlation inverse and then a kernel spectral filter. An alpha exponent on the CORRELATION matrix is a weaker, differently-shaped version of what the filter already does, so it adds nothing and dilutes: the filter keeps the top 150 components, while ev^0.35 keeps all 400 with a smooth decay.
chain_baseline_check: certified reproduces 0.7326 exactly, so these arms are on the certified scale.
